items.title_en: Why "it worked in the demo" is not a delivery standard
items.title_zh: 为何 demo 不是交付,以及为何 evals 是真正的工作
items.body_en:
**Definition**

The demo trap is the gap between an AI system that works on a handful of cherry picked examples and one that works on the messy distribution of real production inputs. A demo is a single performance. Delivery is a system that performs reliably across thousands of varied users, edge cases, and conditions.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Almost every failed enterprise AI project passed its demo. The pattern is so consistent it is almost a law: the system that wowed stakeholders in week 4 falls apart in week 12 when real users send real queries. PMs who can articulate why demos are not delivery, and who insist on evals before scaling, save projects from this trap.

**How it works**

| Demo conditions | Production conditions |
|---|---|
| 5 to 10 cherry picked examples | Thousands of varied, unpredictable inputs |
| Curator knows the right answer | Users do not know what good looks like |
| Run once or twice, take the best | Run every time, no second chances |
| Latency and cost ignored | Latency and cost matter at scale |
| Happy path only | 20 to 30 percent of queries are edge cases |
| Stakeholders are forgiving | Users abandon after one bad answer |

The cognitive trap: humans naturally remember the impressive outputs and discount the misses. A model that works 70 percent of the time looks magical in a 5 example demo (3.5 successes feels great) and unusable in production (30 percent failure rate destroys trust).

**PM decision points**

- Before any production rollout, is there a held out test set of at least 50 to 100 real examples?
- Has the team measured accuracy, not just demoed best cases?
- Is the failure rate acceptable at scale, and what is the cost of each failure?

**Watch outs**

- The most senior person in the room usually anchors on the demo, push back politely with numbers
- "Pilots" often have demo dynamics, friendly users, low volume, forgiving conditions, do not extrapolate
- Stakeholders confuse "the AI is impressive" with "the AI is ready," they are different questions

**Takeaway: a demo proves the system can work, not that it does work. Insist on evals before scaling.**

**Qantas story**

Qantas, like any large enterprise, is vulnerable to the demo trap in AI projects. The pattern unfolds predictably. A team builds a prototype, demos it to senior leadership with five carefully chosen examples, gets enthusiastic approval, and starts the rollout. In production, the same system behaves nothing like the demo, and trust evaporates.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas internal knowledge assistant. The demo includes five questions that the team knows the system handles well: "what is the baggage allowance for international economy," "what are the tier benefits for Platinum," "what time does check in open for international flights." The system answers each one perfectly. Senior leaders are impressed and approve the broader rollout.

In production, the actual distribution of user questions is much messier. Real questions include "my mum needs assistance and a special meal, can we book them together," "I have a Platinum partner who wants to use my benefits on a separate booking, is that possible," "the website says my flight is delayed but the app says on time, which is right." These are not in the polished demo set. The system handles them poorly. Users notice immediately. Word spreads that the AI tool is unreliable. Adoption stalls.

The lesson is that demos are performance, not measurement. A demo with five examples proves the system can work. It does not prove the system does work across the messy real distribution. The gap between demo success and production reality is often 20 to 30 percentage points on completion rate, and the cost of that gap is trust.

The right delivery discipline is to build a real eval set from the start, ideally before the demo even happens. The eval set should include a hundred or more real questions stratified across difficulty, topic, and user type. The system's performance on this set is the real measure. Demos are useful for communication but not for decision making.

The trickier organisational reality is that senior stakeholders often anchor on the demo and resist the eval data. The system worked beautifully in the demo, why are we measuring something else, what is the team hiding? The delivery practitioner's job is to introduce evals as part of the demo itself. The narrative is not "look at these five impressive examples" but "the system handles 87 percent of real production queries successfully, here are examples of the 87 percent and examples of the failures we are working on."

For AI delivery, the broader lesson is that demo discipline is a core delivery skill. Demos are the moment when expectations get set, and badly framed demos set up projects to fail even when the underlying technology is fine. The mature practitioner treats demos as opportunities to introduce honest measurement, not to showcase cherry picked successes. Clients learn to trust the practitioner who can show both the good cases and the failure modes, because that practitioner will not be surprised in production.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

eval (evaluation 的缩写) 是 AI 系统的结构化测试,衡量它在已定义任务上对已定义正确性概念的表现。demo 是展示在精心挑选的输入上工作的系统。Eval 是衡量在代表性输入上工作并产生可重复指标的系统。

**为何在交付中重要**

AI 项目的最大单一失败模式是发布出色 demo 而无可靠 evals 的产品。没有 evals,团队无法回答简单问题: 上周的变更是改善还是损害质量?这个模型变更值得风险吗?系统对生产准备好了吗?Evals 不是花哨的可选附加。它们是 demo 工程和实际产品工程之间的区别。

**运作原理**

eval 套件的关键组件:

| 组件 | 它是什么 | 为何重要 |
|---|---|---|
| 数据集 | 输入 + 预期输出或评分标准的集合 | 真值 |
| 评分者 | 评估输出的代码或模型 | 将质量转换为数字 |
| 指标 | 你跟踪的具体测量 (准确性、引用率、延迟) | 一致的成功定义 |
| 基线 | 当前生产或先前版本的分数 | 让你检测回归 |
| 阈值 | 通过/失败标准 | 让你做出发布决策 |

每次 prompt、模型或检索变更后运行 eval 套件。比较新分数与基线。如果分数下降,在合并之前调查。

**举例,demo 思维 vs eval 思维**

Demo: "看,模型为我们最大的客户写了一封漂亮的电子邮件!"

Eval: "这是 100 个具有代表性客户场景的数据集。我们的电子邮件起草系统对其中 87 个产生符合品牌指南的输出。基线模型符合 81 个。我们的提升是 6 个百分点。延迟相同,成本高 12%。"

**PM 决策点**

- 在第一行代码之前,我们对成功的定义是什么?
- 谁拥有 eval 数据集,它如何随时间演变?
- 我们运行 evals 多频繁,自动化的还是手动的?

**注意事项**

- "看起来不错"评估不可重现,在审查中崩溃
- 由编写代码的同一人编写的 eval 数据集经常错过真实的失败模式
- 公共基准与你的特定用例无关,构建自定义 evals

**要点总结: Evals 将 AI 从 demo 工艺转换为工程学科。不要在没有 eval 套件的情况下发布,期间。**

**Qantas 案例**

eval 的重要性在像 Qantas 这样的航空公司被放大,因为运营环境对不一致毫无容忍度。试点中工作得好的 AI 系统,然后在生产中开始失败,几乎立即失去信任。一旦失去,信任以政治成本而不是工程成本恢复。

考虑用于客户服务的假设 Qantas AI 助手。tooling 提议提交得到批准。第一个 demo 在仔细选择的查询上闪闪发光。"我可以将我的航班改到下周二吗?"产生流畅的响应,正确的政策引用,以及对预订系统的干净工具调用。利益相关者印象深刻。绿灯。生产推出开始。

没有 evals,生产暴露了 demo 没有触及的工作负载: 多段中断恢复、与忠诚度合作伙伴交错的复杂代码共享行程、客户提到的不存在的票价类别、试图使协助提议升级的客户。每天都会有失败模式出现。响应是反应性的,修补 prompts、调整工具描述、希望最好。但没有 eval 套件,团队无法说"这个修复使事情更好,这个使事情更糟"。变更累积,质量随机漂移,信心侵蚀。

具有 evals 的相同推出看起来不同。在范围确定期间,团队构建一组 500 个真实匿名化客户查询,跨越简单查找、复杂行程问题、政策问题、边缘情况,以及测试拒绝行为的对抗性输入。每个都用预期行为标注: 应该调用什么工具,响应应该包含什么,什么应该不在响应中。第一个推出针对该套件运行。基线建立: 简单查询 96% 正确,复杂行程 78% 正确,拒绝行为 100% 正确,平均延迟 2.1 秒。

后续变更被衡量。新 prompt 将复杂行程提升到 85%,但将简单查询下降到 94%。该权衡值得吗?Eval 数据让对话从直觉转向证据。"我们关心的简单类别中没有真实回归,而我们重要的类别中有显著收益,所以是的。"

在 Qantas 规模上有趣的纪律是 eval 套件不断演变。每次生产事件添加一个新案例到套件。每次新功能添加该功能的 evals。eval 数据集变成真值的活资产,代表实际客户范围,而不是发布日数据集的快照。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是 evals 不是工程奢侈品。它们是使 AI 项目可治理的基础设施。具有强 eval 文化的团队在第六个月仍然推动改进。没有它的团队卡在反应性 bug 修复中,从未建立持久信心。客户经常不直接要求 eval 投资,但他们衡量它通过的结果: 减少的事件、更快的功能交付、对发布决策的更高信心。

items.title_en: Eval types: deterministic, LLM as judge, human review, A/B
items.title_zh: Eval 类型: 黄金数据集、LLM 作为评判、人类偏好
items.body_en:
**Definition**

There are four main ways to evaluate AI output quality, each with different cost, accuracy, and use cases. Deterministic evals check for measurable properties (exact match, format validity, presence of citations). LLM as judge uses another LLM to grade output. Human review uses people to grade output. A/B testing compares versions in production with real users.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Picking the wrong eval method wastes money or produces misleading numbers. A team that uses human review for everything spends a fortune and moves slowly. A team that uses LLM as judge blindly trusts numbers that may be wrong. PMs who can match the eval method to the question being asked design eval systems that actually drive decisions.

**How it works**

| Eval type | What it measures | Speed | Cost | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deterministic | Exact match, format, schema, regex, keyword presence | Instant | Free | Structured output, classification, fact lookup |
| LLM as judge | Quality, relevance, tone, factual accuracy (with caveats) | Seconds | Cheap (LLM cost per eval) | Open ended generation, summaries, tone |
| Human review | Anything, gold standard for ambiguous quality | Hours to days | Expensive (USD 0.50 to 10 per item) | Calibration, ground truth, sensitive domains |
| A/B testing | Real user behaviour (clicks, completions, retention) | Days to weeks | Cheap per user, slow to learn | Production decisions, ROI proof |

The right mix is layered. Use deterministic evals for what they can catch (it is free). Use LLM as judge for subjective quality on large samples. Use human review on a smaller calibration set to verify the LLM judge is reliable. Use A/B testing in production for the final word.

**Worked example**

For a customer support chatbot:

- Deterministic: Does every response contain a greeting? Is the response under 200 words? Does it cite a knowledge base article?
- LLM as judge: Is the response factually consistent with the cited article? Is the tone empathetic? Did it answer the user's question?
- Human review: 50 sampled conversations per week, rated by a support lead for trust and accuracy
- A/B testing: Does v2 of the system reduce escalation rate vs v1 in production?

Each layer catches different problems. Deterministic catches format breaks. LLM judge catches quality drift. Human review calibrates the LLM judge. A/B tells you what users actually do.

**PM decision points**

- For each eval question, what is the cheapest reliable method?
- Has the team validated LLM as judge against human review on a calibration set?
- Are deterministic checks running on every output in production, not just in testing?

**Watch outs**

- LLM as judge is biased, judges tend to favour their own model family and verbose responses
- Human review fatigues, reviewers get less reliable after 50+ items per session
- A/B testing without sufficient traffic produces noisy results, calculate sample size needed

**Takeaway: match the eval method to the question. Deterministic for the cheap catches, LLM judge for scale, humans for ground truth, A/B for real world proof.**

**Qantas story**

At Qantas scale, no single eval method is sufficient. The smart approach layers multiple methods based on what each does well.

Consider a hypothetical AI assistant for the Frequent Flyer team. The eval stack might look like this. Deterministic evals run on every response in real time, checking that the output follows expected schema, contains required disclosures, never mentions competitor airline names, and never reveals other members' data. These are free to run, fast, and catch hard failures immediately.

LLM as judge evals run on a sampled subset of production traffic, maybe 5 percent. The judge model evaluates response quality, factual accuracy against retrieved sources, tone consistency with brand guidelines, and helpfulness. The cost is modest per evaluation, the throughput is high, and the results give an ongoing signal of quality drift.

Human review runs on a smaller sample, maybe 1 percent of production traffic, with senior Frequent Flyer team members grading interactions weekly. This is expensive and slow but provides the gold standard against which the LLM judge gets calibrated. If the LLM judge starts diverging from human grades, it needs to be retuned or replaced.

A/B testing happens at the feature level, comparing two versions of the assistant on production traffic. Metrics include user satisfaction ratings, escalation rate to human agents, task completion rate, and follow up question rate. The A/B test gives the business level signal that justifies (or kills) feature releases.

Each layer catches different problems. Deterministic catches schema breaks and policy violations. LLM judge catches quality drift on individual interactions. Human review catches subtle quality issues the LLM judge misses and keeps the judge honest. A/B testing catches whether changes actually improve user outcomes.

The integration is where it gets interesting. The LLM judge runs continuously and surfaces metrics on dashboards. Human reviewers see the highest variance and lowest confidence cases first, focusing their limited time. A/B test results trigger automatic rollback when key metrics regress. Deterministic violations block releases entirely.

The organisational reality is that this stack takes real investment. Many enterprise AI projects ship without it and then struggle in production. The teams that invest in eval infrastructure early ship slower initial versions but improve faster over time, because they actually know when changes help and when they hurt.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that the eval stack is not optional for serious enterprise AI work. The investment pays for itself in faster iteration, fewer production incidents, and clearer evidence to leadership that the system is working. Clients sometimes resist the eval investment because it does not produce visible features. The right framing is that eval infrastructure is what makes future feature work possible. Without it, every change is a guess.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

三种主要类型的 eval 在 AI 项目中实践被广泛使用。黄金数据集 evals 将输出与人工策划的"正确"答案进行比较。LLM 作为评判 evals 使用第二个 LLM 对第一个的输出评分。人类偏好 evals 让人类对真实使用情况下输出的质量评分。每种解决不同的问题,有不同的成本。

**为何在交付中重要**

不同的用例需要不同的 eval 类型。客户问"我们如何衡量 AI 是否在工作?"的答案不是一个。它是基于你测试什么的方法组合。能够将正确的 eval 类型匹配到正确的问题的 PM 节省团队从昂贵的 eval 程序中提取错误的信号。

**运作原理**

| 类型 | 它如何工作 | 最适合 | 成本 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 黄金数据集 | 静态正确答案的语料库,输出自动评分 | 分类、提取、结构化任务 | 低,可重复运行 |
| LLM 作为评判 | 第二个 (通常更强) LLM 评估输出 | 开放式生成,语气,主观维度 | 中,每个 eval 调用都有成本 |
| 人类偏好 | 真实用户或评估者对输出评分或比较输出 | 真正的质量度量,A/B 测试 | 高,慢,但金标准 |
| 启发式 / 基于规则 | 简单代码检查 (格式有效,引用存在,延迟低于阈值) | 不可协商的基本检查 | 几乎免费 |
| 在线 evals | 监控生产输出的特定信号 | 漂移检测,真实世界质量跟踪 | 一旦建立,适度 |

实际上,生产系统使用所有这些。启发式作为入站门 (输出甚至有效吗?)。黄金数据集 evals 用于回归测试。LLM 作为评判用于细微差别。人类偏好用于重大版本里程碑或不确定时。

**举例**

任务: AI 写客户服务响应。

启发式: 响应低于 500 字吗?它使用允许的语气词汇吗?它包括签字吗?

黄金数据集: 对于这个工单类型,响应是否引用正确的政策章节?(自动检查,因为政策引用是结构化的。)

LLM 作为评判: 响应是否符合品牌指南 (温暖、直接、不卑躬屈膝)?(第二个 LLM 对每个响应在 1 到 5 的范围内评分。)

人类偏好: 我们的真实代理评估了 50 个响应,并将它们排名为高于先前模型 73% 的时间。

**PM 决策点**

- 任务是否有客观真值 (黄金数据集) 或主观质量 (LLM 作为评判或人类)?
- 我们能投资多少在 eval 基础设施上,以及在哪里有最高 ROI?
- 我们如何防止 eval 数据泄漏到训练或开发数据中?

**注意事项**

- LLM 作为评判可以变成多数投票,几个不同的评判模型比一个更好
- 人类偏好昂贵且慢,保留它用于不确定不可接受的高风险变更
- 黄金数据集随时间漂移,内容变化,真值变化,在年度审查中预算更新

**要点总结: 没有单一的 eval 方法获胜。匹配类型到问题,组合不同维度的方法。**

**Qantas 案例**

对于像 Qantas 这样的航空公司,不同的 AI 用例为不同的 eval 方法呼喊。考虑组合中的几个,以及哪种 eval 类型适合每个。

为客户服务工单的意图分类是黄金数据集领域。任务是客观的 (每个工单有真正的意图标签),量是高的,真值可以以适度的成本一次构建并定期演变。eval 是确定性的: 模型预测匹配标签百分之多少的时间。回归在每次模型或 prompt 变更后即时被检测。

为延迟通知生成客户面对的电子邮件是 LLM 作为评判和人类偏好领域。这里没有单一正确答案。质量是关于语气、清晰度、品牌一致性、适当道歉,以及包括相关下一步。基于规则的检查可以捕捉基本面 (低于字数限制,提到航班号,避免责备性语言)。LLM 作为评判可以以多个维度对输出评分 (语气适当性,清晰度,完整性)。人类偏好,通过小规模代理审查面板,提供真正的质量度量,但太昂贵无法连续运行。组合不同时间尺度上的所有三个。

代码共享伙伴政策的检索是混合的。"在 SYDLHR 旅行时,我的 BA 持有人状态在 Qantas 上为我提供什么?"这样的问题有真正的答案 (来自代码共享协议),所以黄金数据集 evals 工作良好。但响应是否使其对客户清晰,即使技术上正确,是 LLM 作为评判问题。两种类型并行运行。

为客户服务代理生成响应的 agent 评估是更难的领域。agent 完成任务吗?它使用正确的工具吗?它在适当时升级吗?它产生事实正确的响应吗?它需要分解的复合 eval: 任务完成 (启发式 + 黄金数据集)、工具使用准确性 (黄金数据集)、响应质量 (LLM 作为评判) 和适当升级 (启发式)。一个数字不能告诉你 agent 是否准备好。

有趣的运营点是 eval 类型映射到不同的运营节奏。启发式和黄金数据集 evals 在 CI 中每次提交运行。LLM 作为评判 evals 在每个候选版本上夜间运行。人类偏好 evals 在主要发布之前运行 (太昂贵无法连续运行)。在线 evals 在每个生产响应上的特定信号上持续运行。每个时间尺度捕捉不同种类的问题。

对 AI 交付来说,更广泛的启示是 eval 设计是 AI 项目的工程学科,与系统设计一样有意。"我们将测试它"不是 eval 策略。具体策略命名要回答的问题、要使用的方法,以及要执行的运营节奏。从客户对话的早期带这种特异性的交付从业者赢得信誉,并且通常防止后来扼杀项目的"我们以为它会工作"惊喜。

items.title_en: Building a golden dataset from real client data
items.title_zh: 构建黄金数据集: 从生产流量、合成数据、领域专家
items.body_en:
**Definition**

A golden dataset is a curated collection of representative inputs paired with verified correct outputs (or graded responses), used as the ground truth against which model and prompt changes are measured. It is the foundation of every serious eval system. Without it, "is this better" is a vibe, not a measurement.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Most AI projects do not have a golden dataset. They have a few example queries the team made up, which they re run after every change and call it eval. PMs who insist on building a real golden dataset from real client data create the only mechanism by which improvement can actually be measured. It also exposes scope problems early because building the dataset forces the team to articulate what good looks like.

**How it works**

A practical golden dataset construction process:

1. **Sample real inputs**: pull 100 to 500 actual queries, documents, or interactions from production or pilot data. Stratify across user types, query types, and difficulty.
2. **Label correct outputs**: have a subject matter expert produce or verify the right answer for each input. This is the slow part.
3. **Cover failure modes**: deliberately include known hard cases, edge cases, ambiguous queries, and adversarial inputs.
4. **Lock it down**: version the dataset, freeze it, do not change it during development.
5. **Hold some out**: split into train, validation, and test. The test set is touched only when promoting a change to production.

| Dataset slice | Typical size | Purpose | Touch frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Smoke test | 5 to 10 examples | Quick sanity check during prompt iteration | Every change |
| Validation set | 50 to 200 examples | Tuning prompts, models, retrieval | Daily during dev |
| Test set | 100 to 500 examples | Final pre production evaluation | Only on release |
| Production sample | Ongoing | Continuous quality monitoring | Weekly or daily |

The biggest mistake: building the dataset from synthetic examples or curated demo cases. The dataset must reflect real production distribution, or it lies.

**PM decision points**

- Does the project have a real golden dataset, or just example queries someone wrote up?
- Who is qualified to label correct outputs, and what is the budget for their time?
- Is the dataset stratified across query types, or are 90 percent of examples the easy case?

**Watch outs**

- Dataset contamination, never let the model see test data during prompt iteration, or you measure memorisation not capability
- Stale datasets, refresh quarterly as user behaviour and content evolves
- Synthetic data is fine for augmentation, dangerous as the only source

**Takeaway: a golden dataset is the difference between measured progress and vibes. Build it from real data, lock it down, run it on every change.**

**Qantas story**

A golden dataset is the single most underinvested element of most enterprise AI projects, and Qantas would not be an exception. The temptation is to skip it because building it is slow, expensive, and unglamorous. The cost of skipping it is months of guesswork and rework.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas customer service AI project. The team wants to ship a chatbot that handles routine inquiries. The naive approach is to build the chatbot, do some informal testing, and ship. The disciplined approach is to first build a golden dataset of 200 real anonymised customer inquiries, each paired with the response a senior customer service agent would write. This takes three weeks and AUD 25K in agent time to assemble.

Once the dataset exists, every subsequent decision becomes data driven. Which model to use? Run all candidates against the dataset and pick the one with the best quality at acceptable cost. Which prompt to use? Test prompt variations against the dataset and pick the winner. Which retrieval strategy? Compare retrieval configurations against the dataset and pick the best. The dataset replaces opinion with measurement.

The interesting design questions in dataset construction are non trivial. The 200 inquiries need to be stratified across topic (rebooking, refund, baggage, frequent flyer, special assistance, codeshare, status query, complaint), difficulty (simple lookup vs complex multi step reasoning), customer tone (calm, frustrated, formal, informal), and customer mix (high status, leisure traveller, business traveller, first time customer). The dataset needs to look like real production traffic, not like a polished test suite.

The dataset needs to be split. A smoke test of 10 examples for daily iteration, a validation set of 80 examples for prompt tuning, a test set of 110 examples kept locked away and used only when validating a release candidate. Without the split, the team will tune the system to perform well on the dataset specifically and discover in production that it does not generalise.

The dataset also needs ongoing curation. Customer behaviour shifts over time, new products launch, new policies come into effect. A dataset built in Q1 starts to drift from production reality by Q3. Quarterly refresh cycles, adding new examples from current production traffic, keep the dataset honest.

The organisational reality is that building this dataset requires senior customer service team time, which is expensive and scarce. The investment looks like overhead at the time. The payoff is that every subsequent technical decision is faster, cheaper, and better informed.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that golden datasets are the single highest leverage investment in serious AI delivery work. The clients who appreciate this are the ones who have shipped AI without a dataset previously and discovered the cost. Walking a new client through the dataset construction in week one of a project sets the foundation for everything that follows. It also signals that the team is serious about measurement, which builds credibility with stakeholders who have seen vendors over promise and under deliver.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

黄金数据集是带预期正确输出注释的 AI eval 的代表性输入集合。它是大多数严肃 AI 工程的真值锚。构建好的黄金数据集是 AI 项目交付的最受低估的方面之一。

**为何在交付中重要**

eval 的质量上限是黄金数据集的质量。糟糕的数据集 (太小,不具代表性,有错误的标签) 产生看起来精确但毫无意义的 evals。好的数据集很难构建,需要领域专业知识、迭代和持续维护。提前对此投资的 PM 节省团队从在不可信 evals 上发布的痛苦。

**运作原理**

| 来源 | 它如何工作 | 优势 | 劣势 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 生产流量样本 | 取真实查询样本,人类标注它们 | 真实分布,真实边缘情况 | 私有数据问题,需要标注努力 |
| 合成数据 | 使用 LLM 生成代表性输入 | 快速,可控覆盖,无 PII | 可能错过真实失败模式 |
| 领域专家创建 | SME 编写代表他们看到的查询 | 高质量,带专家直觉 | 慢且贵,有限的多样性 |
| 历史人类决策 | 找到已经做出的人类决策记录 | 已经标注,大体积 | 真值可能不可靠,旧 |
| 对抗性 | 故意构造可能失败的输入 | 推出前发现失败模式 | 不代表正常使用 |

正确的混合通常涉及多个来源。一个生产代表性 100 到 500 个项目的核心。一个边缘情况和拒绝场景的 50 到 100 个对抗性项目。从特定客户区段的 50 到 100 个合成项目,可能在生产中代表性不足。

经验法则: 至少 100 个项目使 eval 数字稳定 (噪音降低)。低于 50 个,运行之间的方差可能掩盖真实变化。

**PM 决策点**

- 数据集如何接近真实生产分布?
- 谁标注它,他们的注释是一致的吗?
- 它如何随时间演变,谁拥有它?

**注意事项**

- 工程师创建的合成数据集错过工程师没有想到的真实失败模式
- 标注一致性需要校准, eval 数据集的两个不同人不应分歧 20%
- eval 集泄漏到训练或 fine tuning 数据中使 eval 无意义,严格保持分开

**要点总结: 黄金数据集是 AI 工程基础设施。投资于它们,治理它们,让它们随生产演变。**

**Qantas 案例**

构建黄金数据集是 Qantas 假设客户服务 AI 系统中最高杠杆的活动之一。它不是华丽的工作,但它是大多数 eval 价值产生的工作。

考虑客户服务意图分类用例。第一遍可能涉及客户服务运营团队的人员花费一周从过去三个月的真实工单中抽取 800 个匿名化工单,代表自然量分布 (重新预订占主导,退款下一个,等等)。一名高级代理标注每个工单的真实意图、紧急程度,以及它是否需要升级到人类。一个不同的高级代理独立标注 200 个工单的子样本,以衡量评估者间一致性。

第一遍数据集足够好开始,但有空白。罕见的意图代表性不足。某些地理区域 (国际客户) 代表性不足。某些时间段 (重大中断) 代表性不足。新兴问题 (新机舱产品的客户问题) 完全缺失。所有这些都需要在数据集中,以便 evals 真正衡量生产性能。

第二遍补充。从代表性不足的细分中策划添加 200 个工单。从需要拒绝的对抗性输入中合成添加 50 个。从历史中断添加 100 个边缘情况,在那里政策应用了不寻常的规则。专家审查整个集合,平衡分布,标准化标签格式。

数据集变成活资产。每次代理发现生产中令人困惑的工单,他们将其添加到队列以供数据集包含。每次新政策推出,新工单类别被添加。每个季度,审查发生,标签随政策变化更新,过时项目被退休。维护成本很小,但持续。

类似数据集存在于每个主要用例: 工程问答的 300 个问题,带专家验证的答案。Frequent flyer 政策上的 400 个问题,带政策映射。延迟通知场景的 200 个场景,带品牌团队验证的"好"响应。每个由拥有该领域的相关 SME 团队维护。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是黄金数据集是 AI 项目内容工作和工程工作的交集。两者都不能单独建造它们。需要工程纪律 (版本控制、对训练数据的隔离、可重复运行) 和内容纪律 (代表性抽样、SME 标注、随生产演变)。从一开始就明确投资于数据集创建的项目以那些把它当作事后想法的项目无法做到的方式扩展。一个能够引导客户通过有意的数据集策略的交付从业者建立了一个超越任何单一 AI 项目的资产。

items.title_en: Regression testing when you change prompts or models
items.title_zh: 回归测试: 当模型 (或 prompt) 变化时捕捉损坏
items.body_en:
**Definition**

Regression testing in AI systems means running the golden dataset against the system after every meaningful change (prompt edit, model swap, retrieval tweak, tool change) to catch quality drops before they ship. It is the same concept as software regression testing, but the surface area is bigger because every component affects every other component.

**Why it matters in delivery**

AI systems are uniquely prone to silent regressions. A prompt change that fixes one issue often breaks two others. A model upgrade improves average quality but regresses on edge cases. Without regression testing, these silent regressions accumulate over months and the system slowly gets worse while the team thinks they are improving it. PMs who instil a discipline of regression testing prevent the slow death by a thousand small changes.

**How it works**

A practical regression workflow:

1. Run smoke test (5 to 10 examples) after every prompt iteration during dev
2. Run validation set (50 to 200 examples) before merging changes
3. Run test set (full golden dataset) before any production release
4. Compare results to baseline, flag any drop in pass rate or score
5. Investigate regressions: which examples got worse, why, is the trade off acceptable?
6. Either fix the regression or document it as accepted

| Change type | Regression risk | Required test |
|---|---|---|
| Minor prompt wording | Medium | Validation set |
| Adding new instructions | High | Validation set, possibly test set |
| Model swap (same family) | High | Full test set |
| Model swap (different provider) | Very high | Full test set, possibly new evals |
| Retrieval parameter change | High | Validation set with retrieval focused queries |
| Tool addition or change | High | Validation set covering tool use cases |

Regression testing should be automated, not manual. CI pipelines that block merges on eval regressions are standard in mature teams.

**PM decision points**

- Is regression testing automated, or does it depend on someone remembering to run it?
- What is the threshold for an acceptable regression, where do we draw the line?
- How are regressions tracked over time, are we slowly drifting down?

**Watch outs**

- LLM as judge variance, the same input can score slightly differently across runs, set tolerance bands
- Cherry picked rollouts, deploying a change that works on the dataset but fails on new patterns the dataset does not capture
- Stale baselines, recalibrate after major changes, not every minor one

**Takeaway: regression test every change, automate it, and treat eval regressions like broken tests. Silent drift is the slow killer.**

**Qantas story**

Regression testing for AI systems is something Qantas would learn the hard way the first time a "small prompt change" silently breaks production. The pattern is universal: a team makes a change they think is minor, ships it without rerunning the eval set, and discovers days or weeks later that some behaviour has degraded.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas customer service assistant where the team updates the system prompt to handle a new fare class introduction. The change adds two sentences about how the new fare class interacts with frequent flyer benefits. It looks like a strictly additive change. The team ships without rerunning the eval set, because "we only added text, we did not change anything existing."

In production, the team starts seeing complaints that the assistant is suddenly worse at handling Platinum status questions, an unrelated topic. Investigation reveals that the new sentences about fare class interaction subtly shifted the model's attention patterns, and a category of Platinum questions that previously worked well now produces less precise answers. The change was not strictly additive in its effect, even though it was strictly additive in its text.

If the team had run the regression suite, they would have caught the regression before ship. The eval set includes Platinum benefit questions, and the regression would have shown up immediately. Instead, they shipped and learned about it through customer complaints, which is a much more expensive way to find out.

The discipline that prevents this is automated regression testing as part of every release. The eval suite runs on every prompt change, every model swap, every retrieval configuration change, every tool change. Releases are blocked if regression exceeds tolerance. Tolerances are set conservatively (no more than one or two percentage point drop on any major category, no drop on critical categories like safety adjacent questions).

The interesting failure modes are around tolerance tuning. Set tolerances too tight and the team cannot ship anything because LLM as judge has some inherent variance. Set tolerances too loose and small regressions accumulate over time, slowly degrading the system. The right discipline is tight tolerances on the critical metrics (where a regression would be a real problem) and slightly looser tolerances on general metrics (where some noise is expected). The tolerances themselves need to be reviewed quarterly.

The other failure mode is regression suite staleness. The eval set built in Q1 might not cover behaviour that became important in Q3 (like the new fare class). The suite needs to grow as the system grows. New use cases added to the system mean new eval examples added to the suite.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that regression testing is what turns AI delivery from craft into engineering. Without it, every change is a guess. With it, the team can iterate quickly with confidence. The clients who appreciate this are the ones who have shipped AI without regression testing previously and seen the slow drift. The clients who resist this often have not seen the slow drift yet, and the right move is to show them what it looks like by running their existing system against a freshly built eval set. The results are usually sobering.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

回归测试是在变更后重新运行 evals 以确认先前工作的事情仍然工作的实践。在 AI 中,这适用于模型版本变更、prompt 编辑、工具变更、检索调整,以及供应商更新。回归测试是 evals 在 AI 项目中获得大部分实际杠杆的地方。

**为何在交付中重要**

AI 系统每周变化,有时每天。每次变化都有破坏先前工作的事情的可能性。在传统软件中,单元测试捕捉这些。在 AI 中,evals 起着相同的作用。没有回归测试,团队随机将错误推送到生产中,客户在工程师之前发现它们。

**运作原理**

回归测试 AI 系统的基本模式:

1. 维护稳定的 eval 数据集 (黄金 + 对抗性 + 边缘情况)
2. 在生产中记录该数据集上的当前基线分数
3. 任何重大变更后,在数据集上运行系统
4. 比较新分数与基线
5. 如果分数下降,在合并之前调查

| 变更类型 | 风险 | 推荐的 eval 节奏 |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt 编辑 | 高 (微小变更可能产生大影响) | 完整套件,在合并之前 |
| 模型版本升级 | 高 (旧 prompt 可能行为不同) | 完整套件 + 扩展边缘情况 |
| 检索变更 (新 chunking、不同 reranker) | 高 (静默检索质量下降) | 检索质量子集 + 端到端 |
| 工具变更 | 中 (新工具可能改变 agent 行为) | 工具相关子集 + 端到端 |
| 配置调整 (温度,top p) | 中 | 完整套件 |
| 监控仪表板变更 | 低 (无功能影响) | 跳过 evals |

回归阈值: 大多数生产团队设置政策,如核心 evals 上的 3% 回归阻止合并,2% 触发审查,1% 在监控仪表板中标记。

**PM 决策点**

- 哪些变更需要哪种 eval 级别? (你不能在每次提交时运行完整套件,但你必须在重大变更时运行)
- 谁拥有 eval 套件,以及在变更暴露空白时谁更新它?
- 当主要供应商升级模型时会发生什么?(很少有团队为此做好准备)

**注意事项**

- "看起来一样"主观,客户的小变更可能在 50% 的项目上更改输出但在 eval 上没有
- eval 套件本身随时间漂移,确保它们仍然代表真实生产
- 提供商可能在没有警告的情况下弃用模型,迫使紧急的 eval 周期,提前计划

**要点总结: AI 系统不断变化。回归测试是使变更安全的工程实践。永远不要在没有它的情况下推送 prompt 或模型变更。**

**Qantas 案例**

在像 Qantas 这样的航空公司,回归测试是 AI 系统在生产中赢得信任并保持信任的纪律。考虑客户服务 AI 助手的运营生命周期。

在最初推出的头几个月,变更频繁。新政策被推出,新功能被添加,新边缘情况被发现,prompts 改进以处理它们。每次变更都有打破已经工作的事情的可能性。回归测试是防止那种倒退侵蚀信任的盔甲。

模式可能如下工作。CI 系统在每个 pull request 上运行核心 eval 套件 (大约 300 个项目跨主要用例)。运行需要五分钟,自动报告结果到 PR。如果分数下降超过 2%,合并被阻止,直到调查。这捕捉大多数显眼的回归。

完整套件 (1,500 个项目跨所有用例,包括对抗性) 夜间运行,有更多时间。它捕捉子集错过的细微回归。结果发布到内部仪表板,可以被生产负责人审查。任何夜间分数下降都触发早晨调查。

模型升级被特别小心对待。当 Anthropic 推出 Claude 的新版本时,系统不是自动升级。相反,新模型在完整 eval 套件上并排针对当前模型运行。性能跨维度比较。回归被分析。所以经常,模型升级在总体上改善质量,但损害特定类别。决定权衡是产品决定,而不是模型决定。

供应商不可避免的弃用是更难的运营挑战。当模型版本被宣布弃用时,有 6 到 12 个月的时间窗口在它停止工作之前。eval 套件让 Qantas 在该窗口期间评估替代模型的能力,并选择最佳替代品,而不是被时间表抢先。

类似的纪律应用于检索变更。当内容团队更新政策文档时,检索 evals 检查相关查询仍然检索正确的政策。当新 chunking 策略被尝试时,检索质量评估系统地。当 vector DB 升级被规划时,索引迁移在 staging 中针对 eval 套件验证。

有趣的失败模式是阐明 "我们不需要为这次变更运行 evals"。当变更感觉很小时压力出现。"我们只是更改了 system prompt 中的一个词。""我们只是从 Claude Sonnet 升级到 Claude Sonnet 改进。""我们只是调整了 reranker 阈值。"每个这样的变更看起来无害,但每个都有惊人的影响。专业团队尽管直觉运行 evals,有时被结果惊讶。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是回归测试纪律是分离的能在 AI 系统上长期可持续运营的团队与生活在反应性救火中的团队。每个 PM 都应能够回答"在合并我们的最后 10 个变更之前,我们运行了什么 evals"。如果答案是"我们对它们感觉良好",而不是"我们运行了这些套件并审查了结果",项目正在为后来的痛苦事件构建。回归测试是机会主义的工程,不是宁愿的。

items.title_en: Online evals: monitoring production quality over time
items.title_zh: 在线 evals 和生产监控: 衡量真正发生了什么
items.body_en:
**Definition**

Online evals are quality measurements done on live production traffic, as opposed to offline evals run on a fixed dataset. They include sampling and grading real user interactions, tracking proxy metrics (escalation rate, thumbs down, retry rate), and detecting drift over time. Online evals are how you know the system is still working, not just how it was working at launch.

**Why it matters in delivery**

AI systems degrade in production for reasons offline evals do not catch: user behaviour shifts, content changes upstream, the model gets a quiet provider update, retrieval index grows or stales. Without online evals, you find out about quality problems from customer complaints, which is too late. PMs who set up online evals catch problems in days instead of months.

**How it works**

| Online eval method | What it catches | Cost | Latency to signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Implicit feedback (clicks, completions, escalations) | Real user behaviour, business impact | Free | Days |
| Explicit feedback (thumbs, ratings, comments) | User perceived quality | Free, but low capture rate | Days |
| LLM as judge on sampled traffic | Quality drift on real distribution | LLM cost per sample | Hours |
| Human review on sampled traffic | High fidelity ground truth | Expensive | Days |
| Distribution monitoring (latency, cost, refusals) | System health, cost blowouts | Free with logging | Minutes |
| Output validation (schema, format, length) | Format regressions | Free | Real time |

A mature online eval setup combines several layers: real time deterministic checks, hourly LLM judge sampling, daily human review on a small sample, and weekly business metric review.

The point is not to grade every interaction. It is to sample enough to detect drift, with a fast feedback loop when something breaks.

**PM decision points**

- What are the leading indicators (escalation, thumbs down, refusal rate) that signal quality problems?
- Who owns the online eval dashboard, and how often is it reviewed?
- What is the threshold that triggers investigation, and who responds?

**Watch outs**

- Sampling bias, if you only review the easy interactions, you miss the hard ones
- Alert fatigue, set thresholds that are meaningful, not just sensitive
- Privacy and compliance, production data in eval pipelines often crosses legal lines, design for it

**Takeaway: offline evals tell you what shipped. Online evals tell you what is still working. Both are required.**

**Qantas story**

Online evals are how Qantas, or any enterprise, would actually know its production AI system is still working. Offline evals tell you what shipped. Online evals tell you what is happening right now.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas customer service assistant six months into production. Offline evals are still passing. The team has not made any prompt or model changes. By every measure they look at directly, the system is fine. And yet escalation rates from the AI to human agents have crept up over the past three weeks from 14 percent to 19 percent. The team only notices because someone glances at the dashboard and the trend line catches their eye.

Investigation reveals that the underlying frequent flyer program had recently changed several benefit rules, and the AI's knowledge base had not been updated. Retrieval was returning stale content that conflicted with what customers were now told elsewhere. The system was confidently giving wrong answers, and customers were escalating to humans to get the correct ones.

This is exactly the kind of problem that online evals catch and offline evals miss. The offline eval set was built before the benefit change. It still passes because it tests against the old (and now incorrect) ground truth. The problem only shows up in production because customers ask questions that depend on the updated rules.

The online eval stack that catches this kind of drift looks like the following. Real time deterministic checks (every response follows schema, never mentions disallowed content). Hourly LLM as judge sampling on a percentage of production traffic, scoring quality and flagging anomalies. Daily human review on a smaller sample, with reviewers focusing on the lowest quality automated grades. Weekly review of business metrics (escalation rate, satisfaction scores, repeat contact rate) at the topic level so trends become visible.

The dashboard that surfaces all of this is critical. If the data is collected but nobody looks at it, the system is no better than not collecting it. The discipline is that someone is responsible for reviewing the dashboard at a defined cadence, with documented triage paths when something looks off.

The interesting design question is how to surface signals without alert fatigue. Set thresholds too sensitive and the team gets paged constantly for noise. Set them too loose and real problems slip through. The right approach is tiered. Hard limits trigger immediate alerts (cost overrun, policy violations). Trend changes trigger weekly review (escalation rate creeping up, quality score drifting down). Aggregate health metrics inform monthly leadership review.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that production AI systems are not static, and the monitoring discipline needs to reflect that. Content changes upstream. User behaviour evolves. Model provider updates ripple through. Without online evals, the team learns about problems from customer complaints, which is slow and expensive. With online evals, the team catches drift in days and addresses it before customers feel the impact. Clients sometimes resist the investment because it does not produce visible features. The right framing is that online evals are how the team protects the investment in features they have already built.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

在线 evals 是衡量实际生产输出质量的连续测量,与衡量精选数据集上质量的离线 evals 形成对比。在线 evals 包括延迟、成本、用户反馈、行为信号 (用户重新表达问题?升级到人类?接受响应?) 和样本驱动的人类审查。

**为何在交付中重要**

离线 evals 告诉你系统的能力。在线 evals 告诉你它实际上正在做什么。两者都需要,因为生产分布与 eval 数据集不同,生产行为漂移,真实用户互动揭示了 eval 数据从未捕捉的失败模式。

**运作原理**

| 在线信号 | 它衡量什么 | 它如何被收集 |
|---|---|---|
| 延迟分布 (p50, p95, p99) | 用户感知的速度 | API 仪器 |
| 成本每请求和每用户 | 实际经济学 | 跨 LLM 调用的 token 跟踪 |
| 用户反馈 (拇指,评分) | 显式质量信号 | UI 提示 |
| 行为信号 (重新表达,放弃) | 隐式质量信号 | 会话分析 |
| 升级率 | 系统何时挣扎 | 人工切换检测 |
| 拒绝率 | 系统拒绝多频繁 | 在响应中模式匹配 |
| 模型置信度分布 | 检测漂移到困难案例 | 日志记录 logprobs 在可用时 |
| 样本人类审查 | 真实质量度量 | 随机抽样 + 标注 |

样本审查是大多数昂贵的金标准信号。1% 的生产输出每周由人类审查者评分。趋势浮现在仪表板中。新失败模式被发现并添加到 eval 套件。这就是生产闭环到离线 eval 改进的方式。

**PM 决策点**

- 我们今天在生产中测量什么,什么是空白?
- 我们如何处理用户反馈,它实际上塑造决策吗?
- 谁审查样本输出,他们的发现如何在产品中行动?

**注意事项**

- 拇指向下数据非常嘈杂,使用模式,不是单个事件
- 行为信号 (重新表达,放弃) 解释起来微妙但常常比显式评分更有信息
- 完整事件日志记录是 GDPR 和数据保留考虑,提前与隐私设计

**要点总结: 在线 evals 关闭离线 evals 和真实生产之间的循环。两者都需要,他们衡量不同的事情。**

**Qantas 案例**

在线 eval 在 Qantas 设置中以揭示离线 eval 错过的事情的方式有价值。考虑客户服务 AI 助手在头几个月的生产中。离线 evals 看起来很棒。延迟在预算内。系统通过它的回归测试。但客户服务运营领导报告"事情感觉不对"。代理沮丧。客户调查显示满意度下降。

在线 evals 揭示离线套件错过的内容。延迟分布在某些时间窗口期间显示长尾,与峰值时段相关,在那里客户被烦恼的等待时间影响。每客户成本比模型显示得更高,因为某些用例迭代多次以解决,模型从未估计的事情。升级率比预期高,因为系统在它本应处理的案例上礼貌地拒绝。拒绝率比预期高,因为模型对模糊但合法的请求被过度警惕。

每个发现来自在线信号,不是离线评估。每个反馈到产品改进。延迟修复涉及在峰值时段路由到更便宜的模型层级。每客户成本修复涉及在缓存中失败时改进检索回退。升级率修复涉及在边缘情况上更宽松的 prompt。拒绝率修复涉及澄清 prompt 中适当的拒绝边界。

样本人类审查程序是更不舒服的纪律。每周 1% 的随机抽样面向客户响应被高级代理审查,在五点量表上评分。评分按用例类别报告。它揭示真实生产质量随时间的演变。

有趣的洞察来自将在线信号与离线 eval 分数相关联。当用户报告满意度下降时,样本审查显示什么?这些发现是否被反映在离线 evals 中?如果不是,套件需要更新以包括类似的案例。如果是,离线 evals 是预测性的,变更应该已经被识别。

第三种纪律是仪表板。在线 evals 不能只存在于日志中。它们必须存在于产品所有者每天看到的仪表板中。延迟、成本、用户反馈、升级率、拒绝率、按类别质量评分 - 所有都可见,所有都按时间趋势,所有都按用例细分。仪表板对生产 AI 与对其他生产系统一样必要。

对 AI 交付来说,要点是 evals 是分层的运营纪律。离线 evals 是更改控制层。在线 evals 是真实质量层。结合它们,他们让团队信心地运营生产 AI。单独,他们留下大空白。建立这两层的客户在六个月内看到改进的轨迹。只有一个的客户看到不可解释的波动,通常将其归因于"AI 不可靠"而不是不完整的衡量。

subtitle_zh: 参考栈、编排、托管、延迟、可观察性

items.title_en: The reference stack: model API, orchestration layer, vector store, app, observability
items.title_zh: 参考栈: 模型 API + 编排 + 向量 DB + 工具 + 监控
items.body_en:
**Definition**

The reference stack is the standard architecture for production enterprise AI applications. It has five layers: the application (what users see), the orchestration layer (the AI logic), the model layer (LLM API or hosted model), the data layer (vector store, knowledge base, tools), and the observability layer (logging, tracing, monitoring). Almost every serious AI product follows some version of this.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Knowing the reference stack lets you scope projects accurately, ask the right architecture questions, and spot when something is missing. PMs without this mental model accept architecture diagrams they cannot evaluate, miss critical components like observability until production, and let teams over engineer layers that did not need to be custom.

**How it works**

```
[User]
   -> [Application layer]       <- Web app, mobile, Slack, Teams, embedded UI
   -> [Orchestration layer]     <- The "AI logic": prompts, agent loops, tool routing
   -> [Model layer]             <- LLM API call or self hosted model
   -> [Data + tools layer]      <- Vector store, databases, APIs, tools
   -> [Observability layer]     <- Logging, tracing, evals, cost monitoring (spans all layers)
```

| Layer | What it does | Common choices |
|---|---|---|
| Application | User interface, auth, session, business logic | Next.js, React, native mobile, Slack bot, Teams app |
| Orchestration | Prompt templates, agent loops, tool routing, state | Custom code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, n8n |
| Model | The actual LLM | Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, self hosted |
| Data and tools | Knowledge sources, function calling targets | Pinecone, pgvector, Postgres, internal APIs |
| Observability | Logs, traces, eval results, cost dashboards | Langfuse, Helicone, Arize, custom Datadog setup |

The biggest scoping mistake is treating this as a 6 week project to build "AI features." It is a full stack engineering project where the AI is one layer.

**PM decision points**

- Is every layer accounted for in the architecture diagram, especially observability?
- Which layers are custom vs framework vs SaaS, and is each choice justified?
- Who owns each layer, and where are the integration boundaries?

**Watch outs**

- Teams over invest in orchestration frameworks early and regret it, start with simple custom code
- Observability is almost always added too late, build it in from day one
- Cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, Google) increasingly bundle multiple layers, evaluate the trade off

**Takeaway: the AI is one layer of a five layer stack. Scope all five from the start.**

**Qantas story**

At Qantas, building any enterprise AI capability would mean working through all five layers of the reference stack, and the most common scoping mistake is treating the AI as if it is one layer instead of one component within all five.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas frequent flyer assistant. The naive scope says "build an AI chatbot for frequent flyer members." Six weeks, two engineers, one product manager. The realistic scope walks through each layer.

The application layer needs an interface for members, which probably means integration with the Qantas app and the website. That is front end engineering, identity integration with the Qantas member auth system, session management, and analytics instrumentation. Realistically three to four weeks of work.

The orchestration layer handles prompt management, conversation state, tool routing, error handling, and rate limiting. For a serious production system this is custom code with proper testing, not framework glue. Two to three weeks.

The model layer is the LLM API call, but it includes the provider relationship (Claude on Bedrock, given the AWS agreement), the region configuration (Sydney for data residency), the rate limit management, and the fallback logic when the primary model is unavailable. Less work in elapsed time, more work in coordination with cloud and procurement teams.

The data and tools layer is the biggest. RAG over the frequent flyer content (which lives across multiple internal systems), tools to read member account state (balance, status, recent activity), tools to check eligibility for specific offers and redemptions, tools to draft member communications. Each tool is an integration with an existing system, with its own access patterns, error semantics, and operational considerations. Realistically six to eight weeks across multiple integrations.

The observability layer captures every interaction with its full context, surfaces dashboards for quality and cost monitoring, feeds the eval pipeline, and supports incident debugging. If built from day one, two weeks. If bolted on after launch, weeks of pain and missed visibility.

The total is 15 to 20 weeks for a real production launch, not the six the naive scope assumed. The AI itself is maybe 20 percent of the work. The rest is integration, infrastructure, monitoring, and the discipline of treating it like a production system.

The mistake teams make is scoping around the visible AI work and discovering the rest later. The discipline is to map all five layers in the initial architecture, allocate time honestly across them, and treat each one as production engineering.

For AI delivery, the broader lesson is that AI delivery is a full stack engineering discipline. The model is exciting and visible, which is why it dominates conversations. The remaining 80 percent of the work is where projects succeed or fail. The mature delivery posture treats the stack as a whole and budgets for every layer. Clients who have shipped AI badly before recognise this immediately. Clients who have not, sometimes need to be walked through it carefully.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

参考栈是大多数生产 AI 系统中存在的标准层。模型 API (Anthropic、OpenAI 等) 提供智能。编排层 (LangChain、LangGraph、自定义代码) 跨步骤协调。向量数据库存储和检索 embedding。工具集成连接到企业系统。监控和可观察性跟踪事情。这五层一起组成几乎每个生产 AI 系统。

**为何在交付中重要**

理解参考栈是 PM 能够对话技术架构而不丢失的方式。它使您能够询问诊断问题 (我们使用什么编排层?我们有什么向量数据库?),做出有意识的供应商决策,并通过其层调试问题。没有它,所有 AI 系统看起来都像黑盒子。

**运作原理**

| 层 | 它做什么 | 流行选项 |
|---|---|---|
| 模型 API | 处理推理调用 | Anthropic、OpenAI、Bedrock、Azure OpenAI、Google AI、Together、Fireworks |
| 编排 | 协调多步流程,处理重试,管理状态 | LangChain、LangGraph、LlamaIndex、自定义代码 |
| 向量数据库 | 存储 embedding,支持语义搜索 | Pinecone、Weaviate、Qdrant、pgvector、Chroma、Bedrock Knowledge Bases |
| 检索增强 | Embedding 模型、reranker、混合搜索 | OpenAI、Cohere、Voyage、内置 |
| 工具集成 | 连接到企业系统 | 自定义 API 包装、MCP、function calling |
| 提示管理 | 版本和测试提示 | 自定义,以及 LangSmith、PromptHub 等 |
| 监控 | 跟踪请求、成本、错误、延迟 | Langfuse、Helicone、Datadog、Honeycomb、自定义 |
| 评估 | 衡量质量随时间 | 自定义,以及 Braintrust、Weights and Biases、Comet |

栈通常布局如下:

```
[用户] -> [应用层] -> [编排层] -> [模型 API]
                                -> [向量 DB] -> [embedding]
                                -> [工具] -> [企业系统]
   [监控/可观察性] 横向 (无处不在)
```

**PM 决策点**

- 我们的栈在每层使用什么,谁拥有每个的运营责任?
- 我们在哪里有供应商锁定,我们何时关心切换?
- 哪些层是托管 SaaS vs 自托管,以及客户的偏好是什么?

**注意事项**

- 框架快速变化,今天的标准明天可能弃用
- 一些客户对每层有现有偏好,提前询问限制
- 监控通常是最后建立的,首先成为大事件,提前预算

**要点总结: 大多数生产 AI 系统是相同的五层。学习栈,使您能够智能地诊断和决定。**

**Qantas 案例**

考虑 Qantas 内部生产 AI 系统的参考栈。从架构上,它将类似于您在其他大型企业中看到的内容,但有航空公司操作约束塑造选择的方式。

模型 API 通过现有云协议消费。Anthropic 的 Claude 通过 AWS Bedcrock。OpenAI 的 GPT 通过 Azure OpenAI。Google Gemini 在它确实赢得位置时通过 Google Cloud。每个模型选择决定是关于哪种现有云关系携带它,而不是直接关系。这避免了新的供应商引入开销。

编排是自定义代码或薄框架使用。Qantas 工程团队倾向于自己构建,而不是采用如 LangChain 这样的重型框架。原因是控制和可调试性。当出现问题时,堆栈跟踪指向团队拥有的代码,而不是不透明的框架内部。许多大型企业都做出相同的选择,在最终离开 LangChain 之前先试用它。

向量 DB 选择基于现有云。对于 AWS 工作负载,Bedrock 知识库或带 OpenSearch 的 pgvector。对于 Azure 工作负载,Azure AI Search。Pinecone 等专业供应商在有令人信服的特定用例时引入,而不是默认。

检索增强使用现成模型供应商。embedding 模型是 OpenAI、Cohere 或 AWS Titan。Rerankers 是 Cohere 或 Voyage,通过云市场。这些是商品决定,不应得到大量架构时间。

工具集成是大多数定制工程发生的地方。Qantas 系统不是 API 优先的。许多核心系统 (预订引擎、frequent flyer 平台、运营调度) 暴露的是 SOAP、专有协议,或没有外部 API。AI 工具的工具集成层通常涉及构建适配器、缓存层和访问控制,这种工程比模型集成多。这一层经常被低估,然后实际占用项目时间的最大部分。

监控和可观察性是经常推迟的层,直到它咬人。一旦系统进入生产,无法分析当出现问题时发生的事情的成本是真实的。成熟的团队从第一天起设置基线的 LLM 调用日志记录、prompt 历史和成本跟踪,即使没有花哨的工具。在 staging 中测试在生产中工作的可观察性,而不是在第一次事件后努力安装它。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是参考栈是企业 AI 系统的共同语言。理解栈,使能够问尖锐的问题: "我们这层使用什么?谁拥有它?它如何被监控?当它失败时会发生什么?"在范围确定中带这种特异性的交付从业者比那些只在抽象级别工作的人更快赢得信任。栈是详细对话发生的基础。

items.title_en: Orchestration frameworks: LangChain, LlamaIndex, n8n, custom, and the tradeoffs
items.title_zh: 编排框架: LangChain、LangGraph、CrewAI,以及"你需要框架吗?"
items.body_en:
**Definition**

Orchestration frameworks are the glue between the model and everything else. They handle prompt templates, tool routing, agent loops, retrieval pipelines, and state management. The main options are LangChain (broadest, most popular, often over engineered), LlamaIndex (focused on RAG), n8n and similar (low code workflow tools), provider SDKs (OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic SDK), and custom code (just Python or TypeScript).

**Why it matters in delivery**

The orchestration framework choice shapes how fast the team can iterate, how easy the system is to debug, and how much lock in there is. The wrong choice creates months of friction. The right choice is often boring: a thin custom layer with explicit code, not a sprawling framework. PMs who can challenge framework choice prevent a common form of over engineering.

**How it works**

| Option | Strengths | Weaknesses | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custom code | Full control, easy to debug, no lock in | Build it yourself | Production systems with clear requirements |
| LangChain / LangGraph | Huge ecosystem, lots of integrations, agent primitives | Complex, abstractions leak, fast moving API | Prototypes, teams familiar with it |
| LlamaIndex | Strong RAG primitives, good document loaders | Less coverage for agents and tools | RAG focused projects |
| Provider SDKs (OpenAI Agents, Anthropic, Vercel AI SDK) | First party, simple, fewer abstractions | Locked to provider, less flexible | Teams committed to one provider |
| Low code (n8n, Zapier, Make) | Visual, business user friendly, fast | Limited for complex AI logic | Workflow automation, internal tools |
| Enterprise platforms (Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce) | Tight integration with existing systems | Lock in, limited flexibility | Enterprises deep in those ecosystems |

The eternal trade off: frameworks promise to speed you up early, then slow you down later. Custom code is slower to start, faster to maintain. Pick based on where the project is in its lifecycle.

**PM decision points**

- Is the project an experiment, a prototype, or a production system, the answer drives the framework choice?
- Does the team have the engineering depth to maintain custom orchestration, or do they need a framework's training wheels?
- How much lock in is acceptable, and can we leave the framework if it goes bad?

**Watch outs**

- Frameworks evolve fast, your code can break on minor version updates
- The first day of a framework is impressive, month six is a different story
- "Everyone uses LangChain" is not a reason, evaluate against your actual needs

**Takeaway: orchestration is glue, not the product. Use the lightest framework that meets requirements, prefer explicit code in production.**

**Qantas story**

The orchestration framework debate plays out at Qantas in predictable ways. Teams new to AI gravitate toward LangChain because it is the most visible option and the documentation is everywhere. Teams that have shipped a few production systems often move away from it.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas internal knowledge assistant. The first version is built on LangChain because the team is learning AI and LangChain has primitives for everything. Eight weeks in, the team is shipping but spending significant time fighting framework abstractions. Debugging is hard because errors come from deep in the framework, not from the team's code. A LangChain version update breaks something subtle that takes three days to diagnose. The framework promised speed and delivered drag.

The team rewrites the orchestration layer in roughly 500 lines of Python around the Anthropic SDK directly. The work takes about a week. The new code is explicit, debuggable, and entirely under the team's control. Error messages are clear. The team's velocity in subsequent weeks is noticeably higher.

The trade off is real. LangChain saved time in the first two weeks, when the team was learning the patterns. It cost time from week three onwards, when the patterns were clear but the abstractions kept getting in the way. The break even point was around four weeks, and the project was scoped for sixteen.

This pattern is so common it is almost predictable. Frameworks promise speed and deliver it in the first sprint. They tax later sprints with abstraction leakage, version compatibility issues, and harder debugging. The right framework choice depends on the stage of the project. Prototypes and proofs of concept benefit from frameworks. Production systems benefit from explicit code.

For AI delivery, the practical lesson is that orchestration frameworks are tools, not commitments. The choice should be driven by the project's stage and the team's depth, not by what is fashionable. For a quick prototype where the team is learning, a framework is fine. For a production system the team will maintain for years, explicit code with the provider SDK is usually better. The provider SDKs (Anthropic, OpenAI Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK) have become much better at handling common patterns, which has narrowed LangChain's value proposition.

The other practical point is that the framework debate is often emotional. Teams that have invested in LangChain defend it. Teams that have been burned by LangChain reject it. The right delivery posture is neither tribal. Evaluate the framework against the project requirements. Pick the lightest option that meets needs. Be willing to swap if the choice turns out to be wrong. Most importantly, do not let framework debates consume time that should be spent on the actual product. The framework is glue, not the product.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

编排框架提供构建 AI 应用的现成组件 (chain、agent、内存、工具、检索器)。LangChain 是市场领导者,最近被 LangGraph (来自同一团队) 用于 agent 工作流补充。CrewAI 专注于多 agent 模式。LlamaIndex 起源于 RAG 但已扩展。还有几十个其他的。问题是您是否需要它们或者更简单。

**为何在交付中重要**

框架选择是一个有声誉的决定,经常默认为"团队听说过的"。错误的框架选择可以放慢交付,在依赖中锁定您,或将复杂性引入您不需要的简单工作流。但避免框架也意味着重新发明轮子。能够清楚地思考权衡的 PM 节省团队从早期错误的多月迁移。

**运作原理**

| 选项 | 适合 | 优势 | 劣势 |
|---|---|---|---|
| LangChain | 通用,RAG,简单链 | 大量集成,大社区 | 重型抽象,API 流失,调试痛苦 |
| LangGraph | Stateful agent,工作流 | 显式状态机模型,可调试 | 学习曲线,LangChain 生态系统依赖 |
| LlamaIndex | RAG 重型工作流 | 强大的检索原语 | 在非 RAG 上较弱 |
| CrewAI | 多 agent | 简单的多 agent 抽象 | 早期成熟度,有限的生产实战 |
| Vercel AI SDK | TypeScript / Next.js 应用 | 流式响应,前端集成 | 限于 JS 生态系统 |
| 自定义代码 | 当您需要控制时 | 没有不可见的抽象,容易调试 | 您构建它,您维护它 |

经验法则: 对于简单的单调用 LLM 应用,使用没有框架的提供商 SDK。对于带 3 到 5 步的 RAG,使用轻量级框架或自定义代码。对于 stateful agents,LangGraph 或自定义。对于复杂的多 agent,仔细评估 CrewAI 与自定义。许多生产团队开始使用 LangChain,然后用自定义代码替换部分。

**PM 决策点**

- 我们的实际复杂性级别是什么?简单 RAG 通常不需要框架
- 团队拥有什么样的工程?对自定义代码舒适与不舒服
- 我们将如何随时间维护这个,框架文档质量如何

**注意事项**

- LangChain 的抽象经常使简单事情变得复杂,有时您 fighting 框架而不是构建
- 框架版本以打破现有代码的方式更改,锁定版本并仔细升级
- 团队经常将"我们使用 LangChain"作为成熟度信号说,使评估更难: 不要被那个信号愚弄

**要点总结: 框架是工具,不是要求。从简单开始,当复杂性证明合理时引入框架。**

**Qantas 案例**

考虑 Qantas 团队在编排框架选择上的对话。压力是显著的。LinkedIn 帖子谈到 LangChain。咨询公司推荐它。一些供应商需要它。开发者社区围绕它建立。诱惑是说"是的,我们使用 LangChain"作为现代化的信号。

诚实的工程评估通常较少令人兴奋。LangChain 的强抽象在 3 步检索增强生成 pipeline 中提供有限的杠杆。同样的工作流可以使用 Anthropic 或 OpenAI SDK 直接以更少的代码实现,更可调试的堆栈跟踪,以及更少的依赖更新。LangChain 提供工具的丰富生态系统,但 90% 是 Qantas 不需要的连接器,5% 与企业要求 (审计、访问控制) 不兼容,5% 是相关的,但可以直接实现。

更微妙的案例是 stateful agentic 工作流。这是 LangGraph 等框架开始证明其复杂性合理的地方。状态机模型与 agent 设计很好地映射。可见性比手动状态管理更好。LangGraph 在像之前讨论的中断恢复 agent 这样的用例中可能确实是合理的选择。

但即使在那里,Qantas 工程团队需要评估的不是框架本身,而是采用它的运营负担。框架版本以打破现有代码的方式更改。新框架版本以已弃用的 API 推出。安全漏洞需要快速升级到不一定向后兼容的版本。当框架社区移动时,留在固定版本上变成技术债务。当社区移动时,升级是工程时间。

替代方案是自定义代码,该代码完全做项目需要的事情而没有更多。这看起来不那么时髦,但带来真实的好处。代码完全是团队拥有的。堆栈跟踪指向他们写的代码。没有不可见的抽象。维护是预算的,而不是被框架版本爆发驱动。

许多大型企业团队的演变模式是开始时使用 LangChain (因为它们已经听说过),随着复杂性增长撞到框架边缘,然后逐渐用自定义代码替换部分,直到框架成为 5% 的代码库。如果您从一开始就知道结局,从自定义代码开始通常是合理的选择,框架仅在它清楚地节省时间和复杂性的特定子工作流中引入。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是框架选择不应基于"现代"的感觉做出。它应基于诚实评估特定工作流的复杂性,团队的工程偏好,以及对供应商和运营的现实评估。能够说"是的,我看到为什么 LangChain 看起来吸引人,这里是我们仔细评估它的方式,这是我们的具体选择以及为什么"的交付从业者比那些只是采用最响亮选项的人更快赢得信任。

items.title_en: Hosting: provider API vs Azure OpenAI vs Bedrock vs self hosted
items.title_zh: 托管 (云原生 vs 直接 API): 重要的实际差异
items.body_en:
**Definition**

There are four main ways to consume LLMs in production. Native provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google direct). Cloud provider hosted versions of those models (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock for Claude and others, Google Vertex). Self hosted open weight models (you run Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek on your own infrastructure). And specialised inference providers (Together, Fireworks, Groq) that host open weights for you on a per token API.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Hosting choice is driven by procurement, data residency, contracts, and unit economics, not by which is "best." Enterprise procurement often forces a specific path before engineering even gets a say. PMs who understand the trade offs can spot the right path early instead of scoping the wrong one and having it overturned in week six.

**How it works**

| Option | What you get | Trade off |
|---|---|---|
| Native provider API | Direct access, fastest features, simplest integration | Separate billing, separate contract, separate data terms |
| Azure OpenAI | OpenAI models on Azure, with Azure data terms and region control | Slight feature lag, Azure procurement, Microsoft contract |
| AWS Bedrock | Claude, Llama, others on AWS, with AWS data terms and IAM | Slight feature lag, AWS procurement, AWS region constraints |
| Google Vertex | Gemini and others on Google Cloud, with GCP terms | Slight feature lag, GCP procurement |
| Self hosted open weights | Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral on your own GPUs or cloud GPUs | Full data control, you run inference, you own ops |
| Inference providers (Together, Fireworks, Groq, OpenRouter) | Open weight models as a managed API | Less mature, fewer enterprise certifications |

The pattern in regulated industries: data residency and existing cloud agreements decide it before AI considerations enter. If the client is an Azure shop, Azure OpenAI is the path of least resistance. If they are AWS, Bedrock. If they need everything to stay on prem, self hosted.

**PM decision points**

- What cloud and AI contracts does the client already have, and which models are accessible through them?
- Are there data residency, sovereignty, or zero retention requirements?
- Does the project need bleeding edge features (native API) or is stable enterprise good enough (cloud hosted)?

**Watch outs**

- New model versions hit native APIs first, cloud hosted versions often lag weeks or months
- Cloud hosted models have different rate limits, quotas, and request formats than native
- Self hosting "for cost reasons" rarely pencils out below 50M+ tokens per day

**Takeaway: hosting is a procurement decision wearing an engineering costume. Find the contractual path first, model the cost second, choose the architecture third.**

**Qantas story**

The hosting decision for any Qantas AI capability is driven by procurement, contracts, and data residency more than by engineering preference. The decision space is narrower than it looks from the outside.

Qantas has deep AWS and Microsoft relationships. Adding Claude via Bedrock or OpenAI via Azure is a procurement amendment, not a new vendor relationship. Direct Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google contracts would require new supplier onboarding, new privacy reviews, new payment processes, and new audit obligations. For a sophisticated procurement function, that is months of work for no technical benefit.

The Sydney region availability matters. Both Bedrock and Azure OpenAI have Sydney region options for the major model families, which satisfies the typical data residency requirements. Without Sydney availability, the conversation gets much harder because data leaving Australia raises additional review steps.

For most Qantas AI workloads, the hosting choice is therefore Claude on Bedrock or OpenAI on Azure, depending on which model family the team needs. Both have the regional presence, both inherit the cloud commercial agreements, and both satisfy the typical compliance posture without additional work.

Self hosting open weight models on Qantas owned infrastructure is technically possible but rarely justified. The use case would need to combine sensitive data (cannot leave the corporate boundary), high volume (needs the unit economics of self hosting), and acceptable quality at smaller model sizes (the workload does not need flagship reasoning). Most workloads fail one of these tests. The narrow exceptions exist (some operational safety data, some specific high volume embedded classification) but they are exceptions, not the default.

Inference providers like Together or Fireworks could host open weights as a managed API, but the procurement work is similar to a new direct provider contract, and the maturity is lower than Bedrock or Azure. For most Qantas use cases, this is not the right path.

The interesting strategic question is how to manage hosting in a multi cloud reality. Most large enterprises have both AWS and Azure for different reasons. A mature AI strategy uses both, with workloads placed based on the team owning them, the existing infrastructure they need to integrate with, and the specific models needed. Forcing all AI into one cloud creates friction and does not save much.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that hosting decisions are procurement decisions dressed in technical language. The right opening question in any scoping conversation is "what cloud and AI contracts does the client already have." The answer narrows the options dramatically, and the architecture conversation flows from there. Trying to push through a technically superior option that does not match the procurement reality wastes weeks for no benefit. The clients who appreciate this are the ones who have seen previous projects stall on procurement issues that were predictable from day one.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

模型 API 可以直接消费 (Anthropic API、OpenAI API、Google AI Studio) 或通过云原生服务 (AWS Bedrock、Azure OpenAI、Google Cloud Vertex AI)。基础模型在每种情况下都相同。差异在于商业合同、数据处理、监控、可用区域,以及它如何融入客户的现有架构。

**为何在交付中重要**

托管选择对应用看起来像什么影响很小,但对项目可以何时启动有巨大影响。它影响采购时间表、数据驻留合规性、合同语言、监控集成,以及部署在哪个云中。选择错误,启动延迟数月。选择正确,项目流畅。

**运作原理**

| 维度 | 直接 API | 云原生 |
|---|---|---|
| 商业关系 | 与提供商的新合同 | 现有云合同 |
| 时间到第一次推出 | 仅在新供应商批准的情况下慢 | 快,在现有协议下 |
| 数据驻留 | 取决于提供商的区域 | 与云区域选择一致 |
| 合规性继承 | 单独的合规审查 | 通常从云协议继承 |
| 监控集成 | 单独的工具或自定义 | 与现有云监控集成 |
| 价格 | 通常稍微便宜 (例如,Anthropic 直接) | 稍微贵 (云加价),但通过现有承诺 |
| 模型可用性 | 最早接触新模型 | 延迟,模型在云上需要时间出现 |
| 高级功能 | 完整 API 表面 | 子集,有些功能仅直接 |

对大多数 ANZ 企业 (Qantas, banks, Telstra),云原生几乎总是默认。新供应商引入数月的工作。云原生消费数天。

**PM 决策点**

- 客户已经有现有合同的云?
- 是否需要的特定高级功能仅通过直接 API 可用?
- 数据驻留要求是否与云区域可用性匹配?

**注意事项**

- 云提供商落后于直接 API,某些功能晚来或永不来
- 价格差异不大,直接的成本节省很少证明合规复杂性合理
- 一些客户对多个云有不同的偏好,对多模型架构需要分别评估每个

**要点总结: 对大多数企业,云原生托管是默认。直接 API 仅在云路径无法工作时需要。**

**Qantas 案例**

托管选择对 Qantas 几乎完全由现有云关系决定。航空公司在核心系统上有 AWS,在生产力和某些工作负载上有 Microsoft。任何新的 AI 工作负载将通过这些云协议之一消费,除非有不可逾越的技术原因不能。

实际优势是直接和重大的。新供应商批准是六个月的工作,涉及多个内部团队 (法务、采购、安全、技术风险、隐私)。云原生消费是一个采购修订,通常需要数周。AI 团队可以在六个月而不是新供应商引入将允许的时间内构建和发布。

数据驻留合规通过区域选择干净地映射。AWS 悉尼区域 (ap southeast 2) 和 Azure Australia East 在用户和澳大利亚监管者眼中具有清晰的数据驻留含义。直接 API 通常通过提供商的全球基础设施路由,该基础设施可能或可能不与澳大利亚驻留要求匹配。

监控集成更好。Qantas 已经使用 AWS CloudWatch 和 Azure Monitor。云原生 AI 调用流入现有可观察性栈。直接 API 调用需要单独的监控基础设施。

价格差异很少证明替代品合理。直接 Anthropic 价格通常是 Bedrock 价格的 5 到 10% 折扣,但仅在云路径无法工作时折扣值得新供应商负担。对于大多数工作负载,Qantas 接受云加价。

直接 API 赢得位置的情况很窄。一些功能首先在直接 API 上推出 (例如,Anthropic 经常在直接 API 上首先推出新模型,Bedrock 跟随数周或数月)。如果团队需要昨天的新模型,直接 API 可能短暂地证明合理。但通常,等待云可用性是更便宜的选择。

另一个潜在的直接 API 案例是非常高量的工作负载,价格差异变得重要。在每月数百亿 tokens,5% 折扣是真正的钱。但很少 Qantas 工作负载实际操作在该量,所以这是理论而不是实践。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是托管选择是采购对话,而不是工程对话。来自客户对话早期带这种理解的交付从业者可以快速将正确的架构对准。"我们将使用 Anthropic 的 Claude"是开始。"通过 Bedrock 在 ap southeast 2 区域,使用现有的 Qantas AWS 协议,使用 Anthropic 在 Bedrock 上提供的零数据保留选项"是真实的架构。后者让项目实际启动。

items.title_en: Latency, streaming, and caching basics
items.title_zh: 延迟、流式传输和缓存,以及客户感觉到什么
items.body_en:
**Definition**

Latency is the time from user request to user visible response. Streaming sends the response token by token as it generates, so the user starts seeing output within a second instead of waiting for the full answer. Caching stores and reuses previous results to avoid repeated model calls. Together, these three determine whether an AI product feels responsive or slow.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Users abandon AI products that feel slow. A 4 second wait for a chatbot reply destroys the perception of intelligence, even if the answer is perfect. PMs who treat latency and caching as performance features, not optimisations to do later, ship products that feel like magic instead of friction.

**How it works**

| Concept | What it does | Typical impact |
|---|---|---|
| End to end latency | Time from user input to final response | 2 to 30 seconds depending on architecture |
| Time to first token | Time until the user sees the first word | 200ms to 2 seconds, the key UX metric |
| Streaming | Tokens delivered as generated | Cuts perceived latency by 50 to 80 percent |
| Prompt caching | Reuse cached portions of long prompts (system prompt, retrieved docs) | 60 to 90 percent cost reduction on cached input, faster too |
| Semantic caching | Match similar queries to past answers | Avoid repeat calls entirely on common queries |
| Output caching | Cache full responses by input hash | Free repeat answers for deterministic tasks |
| Parallelisation | Run independent calls concurrently | Cuts total latency by N for N parallel calls |

The latency budget for a chat interface is roughly: time to first token under 1.5 seconds (excellent), under 3 seconds (acceptable), over 5 seconds (bad). For agentic tasks, users tolerate longer if you show progress.

**PM decision points**

- What is the target time to first token, and is the team measuring it?
- Is streaming enabled everywhere it can be, including in agent intermediate steps?
- Is prompt caching configured for stable system prompts and frequent retrievals?

**Watch outs**

- Streaming complicates error handling, retries mid stream are messy
- Semantic caching can return stale answers when content has changed, set TTLs
- Some providers charge for cached input, some give it free, check terms

**Takeaway: latency is UX. Stream by default, cache aggressively, design for time to first token, not total time.**

**Qantas story**

Latency in a Qantas AI assistant is not a technical metric, it is a user experience metric, and the difference shows up in adoption rates. Consider a hypothetical Qantas customer service AI tool used by agents during live customer calls. The agent is on the phone with a customer, types a question, and needs a response fast enough to use it in the live conversation. Eight seconds is too long. Three seconds is acceptable. One second feels like magic.

The naive architecture sends the full prompt, waits for the full response, and returns it all at once. With a long system prompt, retrieved content, and a model response of moderate length, that is easily eight to twelve seconds. Unusable for live agent support.

Streaming changes the experience. Time to first token drops to under a second, the rest of the response streams in over the next few seconds, and the agent starts reading and using the answer immediately. Same total compute, dramatically better UX. The agent perceives the system as responsive rather than sluggish.

Caching adds more. The system prompt for an agent support tool is large and stable (instructions, tone guidance, refusal patterns, tool descriptions). The retrieved content for a specific topic is also reused across many agents handling similar customer issues. Both are good caching candidates. Provider prompt caching can reduce input cost by 80 percent or more on cached portions, and also speeds up the first token by avoiding redundant input processing.

The interesting design question is what happens during streaming when an error occurs mid response. The user has seen the first few sentences. A graceful failure pattern shows a clear error message and offers a retry. A poor failure pattern leaves the response hanging or cuts to a generic error. The streaming UX needs to be designed end to end, not just enabled as a feature.

The other consideration is when streaming hurts. For programmatic integrations where the consumer is another system that needs the full response, streaming adds complexity for no benefit. The downstream system has to assemble streamed chunks before processing. For these cases, non streaming is simpler.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that latency is a first class product concern, not an optimisation. The decisions about streaming, caching, and parallel calls should be made during architecture design, not after launch when users complain. Clients sometimes ask "is the AI fast enough" and the right response is to walk them through the latency budget for their specific use case and design for it. Agent support tools have one latency profile. Email summarisation has a different one. Batch processing has a third. Treating these the same way produces products that feel wrong in all of them.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

延迟是用户感觉到的从他们输入到他们看到响应的时间。流式传输是模型生成响应时一个 token 一个 token 地发送响应,而不是等待整个响应完成。缓存意味着将以前响应的部分 (整个响应,或检索结果,或 prompt 前缀) 存储以便它们不需要重新计算。三者都驱动用户体验,以及 AI 系统的成本。

**为何在交付中重要**

延迟是大多数面向用户的 AI 产品中最容易被低估的设计因素。10 秒的响应感觉破碎,即使技术上正确。3 秒的流式响应感觉响应,即使生成 7 秒。能够优化整个延迟图的 PM 交付感觉远远好于其他 AI 产品的产品。

**运作原理**

| 因素 | 影响 | 缓解 |
|---|---|---|
| 模型大小 | 较大模型更慢 | 当质量允许时使用较小模型 |
| Prompt 长度 | 较长 prompt 更慢 (输入处理) | 修剪 prompt,使用 prompt 缓存 |
| 响应长度 | 较长响应更慢 (token 生成) | 限制最大 tokens,要求简洁 |
| 检索 | 添加 100 到 500ms | 缓存频繁查询,异步并行 |
| 工具调用 | 每个工具调用是单独的 LLM 调用 + 工具时间 | 最小化工具调用,并行化在可能时 |
| 网络 | 区域,提供商位置 | 选择附近区域 |
| 流式传输 | 不减少总时间,但减少感知时间 | 默认启用 |
| 缓存 | 重复 prompt 或检索的大幅减少 | Prompt 缓存,语义缓存,KV 缓存 |

Prompt 缓存特别强大: 大多数提供商现在让您在多个调用中重用 prompt 的前缀 (例如,稳定的 system prompt 加文档上下文),只对新部分付费。可以削减 80% 的 prompt 处理成本和延迟。

**PM 决策点**

- 这个工作流的延迟预算是什么?(实时聊天 < 3s, 后台工作可以是分钟)
- 流式传输是否启用,以及它对感知的影响是什么?
- 我们在哪里缓存,我们多频繁地缓存命中?

**注意事项**

- 流式传输隐藏长延迟,直到事情变得真正破碎,有时是糟糕的设计选择
- 缓存命中率随时间漂移,提示模板的变更使缓存无效
- 长上下文模型不必更慢,但通常是,基准您的特定提供商

**要点总结: 延迟感觉与原始时间一样重要。流式传输 + 缓存 + 简洁性的组合赢得了大多数 UX 战斗。**

**Qantas 案例**

考虑面向客户的 Qantas AI 助手中的延迟工程。在网站上,客户期望聊天响应在两秒内开始流式传输,并在六秒内完成。任何超过这个的时间感觉破碎,客户放弃。来自移动应用,期望甚至更严格。

天真的实现可能有 12 秒响应。检索花费 400ms,model 调用花费 7 秒来生成 400 token 响应,工具调用增加 3 秒,后处理增加 1.6 秒。每一步是必要的,但总和是糟糕的。

优化路径如下工作。首先,流式传输,以便用户立即开始看到 tokens。这本身将感知延迟从 12 秒减少到 1.5 秒 (到第一个 token 的时间)。即使总生成时间相同,感觉根本不同。

第二,prompt 缓存。客户服务 system prompt 大于 2,000 tokens,跨所有客户调用稳定。在 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 上的 prompt 缓存使该 2,000 tokens 接近免费,并将输入处理延迟从约 200ms 削减到约 30ms。

第三,模型选择。最初的实现使用旗舰模型 (Opus) 处理一切。但对 70% 的简单查询,Sonnet 在质量上无法区分,在延迟上明显更快。路由层将简单查询发送到 Sonnet,复杂查询发送到 Opus,削减大多数交互的延迟。

第四,工具优化。当工具调用是必要的 (查找预订,获取航班状态) 时,它们尽可能并行运行,而不是顺序。同时调用三个工具花费 max(t1, t2, t3) 时间,而不是 t1 + t2 + t3。

第五,响应长度修剪。Prompt 指导对客户问题的简洁响应。"用 2 到 4 句话回答"切断 token 生成时间。模型经常想要冗长,prompt 必须明确目标长度。

放在一起,12 秒响应可能成为 6 秒响应,具有 1.5 秒的感知时间到第一个 token。这是从破碎到响应。

第六个杠杆是缓存,在适当的地方。常见问题 ("什么是行李津贴") 的答案的语义缓存意味着这些不必每次调用模型,即使措辞不同。对于这些查询,延迟下降到亚秒,成本下降到接近零。语义缓存需要谨慎使用,因为微小的措辞差异有时意味着真实的语义差异,但对常见问题它很强大。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是延迟工程是 AI 产品的核心 UX 学科。所有其他面向客户的产品都是如此,但 AI 产品经常忽略它,因为团队在质量和能力上印象深刻并接受任何延迟数字。能够仔细思考延迟图,优化每一层,并在主观感觉和客观测量上交付的交付从业者构建感觉好的产品,而不仅仅是工作的产品。

items.title_en: Observability: logging, tracing, replay (Langfuse, Helicone, Arize)
items.title_zh: 可观察性: prompts、completions、token 数和当出错时的痕迹
items.body_en:
**Definition**

Observability in AI systems is the ability to see what happened inside every interaction: the exact prompt sent, the retrieved chunks, the tool calls made, the model output, the cost, the latency, and the user feedback. Tools like Langfuse, Helicone, Arize, and LangSmith specialise in this for LLM workloads. Generic observability tools (Datadog, Honeycomb) can be configured to do it but require more setup.

**Why it matters in delivery**

Without observability, debugging an AI system is guesswork. When a user complains about a bad answer, you cannot reproduce it, cannot see what went wrong, and cannot prove it is fixed. With observability, debugging takes minutes instead of days, evals can be built from real traffic, and cost can be controlled. It is the single most under invested layer in most AI projects.

**How it works**

| What to capture | Why | Tool support |
|---|---|---|
| Full prompt and response | Reproduce and debug any interaction | All major tools |
| Tool calls and results | Understand agent decisions | Langfuse, LangSmith |
| Retrieval results | Debug RAG quality | Langfuse, Arize, custom |
| Latency per step | Find slow components | All major tools |
| Token counts and cost | Track unit economics | Langfuse, Helicone, Datadog |
| User feedback (thumbs, ratings) | Connect quality to specific interactions | Langfuse, LangSmith |
| Eval scores | Track quality over time | Langfuse, Arize |
| Replay capability | Run an exact past interaction with a new prompt or model | Langfuse, LangSmith |

A typical observability setup wraps every LLM call with a trace that captures all of the above, then exposes it in a dashboard for the team. Mature setups also export to analytics tools for cost forecasting and to eval pipelines for quality monitoring.

**PM decision points**

- Is observability instrumented from day one, not bolted on after launch?
- Can the team replay any production interaction with a different prompt or model?
- Are cost and quality dashboards reviewed weekly, or only when something breaks?

**Watch outs**

- Logging prompts and responses raises privacy and compliance issues, design for redaction
- Observability adds latency if synchronous, batch and stream where possible
- Self built observability is a tempting time sink, use existing tools unless you have a very specific need

**Takeaway: observability is not a nice to have. It is how you debug, how you build evals, and how you control cost. Build it from day one.**

**Qantas story**

Observability is the layer Qantas, or any enterprise, would discover the importance of the hard way the first time a production AI incident happens and the team cannot figure out what went wrong.

Consider a hypothetical Qantas frequent flyer assistant after a few months in production. A senior member complains that the AI told them they had 250,000 points when they actually had 25,000. The complaint reaches the team. The first question is what happened. Without observability, the team can guess: maybe a retrieval error, maybe a model hallucination, maybe a tool integration bug. With observability, the team pulls the exact trace of the interaction in two minutes.

The trace shows the system prompt that was active at the time, the user query, the tool call that was made (a member balance lookup), the response from the tool (which correctly returned 25,000 points), and the model output (which incorrectly said 250,000 points). The model had ignored the tool response and hallucinated a different number. Root cause identified in five minutes. Mitigation: add a deterministic check that the response's point figures match the tool response, and refuse to send if they do not. Deployed within a day.

Without that observability, the team would have spent days trying to reproduce, would have built false hypotheses, and would have left the member with a vague apology and no fix. With it, the team identified the issue, fixed it, and could explain to the member exactly what happened.

The other use of observability is cost analysis. A team running an internal agent for research support discovers their monthly bill is much higher than forecast. With observability, the team filters by task and finds that 70 percent of cost is from a small number of tasks that ran 30+ agent steps each. They identify the pattern, add stricter step limits, and cut cost by 60 percent. Without observability, the same investigation would have been guesswork against aggregate billing data.

The observability stack at Qantas scale needs to capture full prompts, full responses, all tool calls and their results, retrieval queries and returned chunks, token counts and cost per call, latency per step, and user feedback when available. Tools like Langfuse, Helicone, and LangSmith specialise in this. Generic observability tools like Datadog can be configured to do it with more setup. Either way, the investment needs to happen from day one.

The interesting privacy consideration is that observability captures prompts and responses, which often contain PII. The observability layer needs its own redaction discipline, its own access controls, and its own retention policies. This is not a security afterthought, it is part of the design.

For AI delivery, the lesson is that observability is the single most underinvested layer of most enterprise AI projects, and it is the layer that determines whether the team can debug, optimise, and improve over time. Building it in from day one is dramatically easier than adding it after launch. Clients who have shipped AI without observability previously understand this immediately. Clients who have not, sometimes need to see the consequence of running blind for a few weeks to internalise the value.
items.body_zh:
**定义**

可观察性是看到生产中实际发生什么的能力。对于 AI 系统,这意味着每个 LLM 调用的 prompts、completions、token 数、延迟、成本、错误、工具调用,以及多步工作流的完整执行痕迹。没有可观察性,生产 AI 是一个有时返回错误答案的黑盒子。

**为何在交付中重要**

可观察性是 AI 项目中差异化人员的最常见地方。每个团队都说"我们将监控它"。少数人实际上为它构建。当事件袭击 (它们会袭击) 时,具有真实可观察性的团队在分钟内找到原因。没有它的团队在天内找到原因,失去客户信任。可观察性不是奢侈品,它是 AI 在企业中的运营成熟度。

**运作原理**

| 信号 | 什么 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 完整 prompt 和 completion 日志 | 每个 LLM 调用,逐字 | 调试,审计,质量审查 |
| Token 计数 | 每个调用的输入和输出 tokens | 成本归因,容量规划 |
| 延迟分解 | 每步的时间 (检索,模型,工具) | 性能优化 |
| 错误和重试 | 失败,重试,最终结果 | 可靠性跟踪 |
| 工具调用痕迹 | 调用了什么工具,有什么输入,有什么输出 | Agent 调试 |
| 用户上下文 | 用户 ID (脱敏),会话,功能标志 | 范围调查 |
| 评估分数 | 在线评分 (用户反馈,自动检查) | 质量趋势 |
| 模型置信度 | 在可用时,token logprobs | 难度检测 |

工具选项: 开源 (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, Phoenix) 和托管 SaaS (Datadog with LLM observability, Helicone, Braintrust)。许多团队从托管供应商开始,因为速度。

对 prompts 和 completions 的访问需要谨慎设计。它有时是 PII (用户在与 AI 共享个人数据)。它有时是商业敏感的 (Qantas 客户记录,内部文档)。日志保留,访问控制和 PII 编辑需要从一开始就设计。

**PM 决策点**

- 我们今天捕获哪些信号,什么是空白?
- 谁可以查看日志,以什么级别的细节,以多长时间?
- 我们设计了 PII 编辑吗,还是事件后才发现?

**注意事项**

- 仅在事件发生时打开调试日志记录意味着对那个事件没有可观察性
- LLM 调用日志是大的 (每个调用可能是 KB),提前预算存储
- 跨多个供应商 (云,LLM 提供商,工具) 的可观察性集成花费时间,从第一天起规划

**要点总结: 您不能调试您不能看到的东西。可观察性是不可协商的,从第一天起构建它。**

**Qantas 案例**

考虑 Qantas 客户服务 AI 中的可观察性。在最初阶段,团队压力大要快速交付,有时跳过可观察性投资,以更快交付一个"工作"的系统。第一个生产事件揭示了什么时候省略它的成本。

模式可预测地展开。客户报告 AI 助手在特定预订上向他们提供了错误信息。客户服务主管想要调查。"我们能看到 AI 与该客户的对话吗?"团队拼凑日志,但完整的 prompt 和 completion 记录不可用。他们能看到响应,但不能看到提供给模型的检索文档,或者它得到的 system prompt 版本,或者它做的工具调用,或者每步花费的时间。调查停滞。决议涉及向 AI 系统提出关于客户的有教育性问题,并希望可以重现行为。它经常不能。

带强可观察性的相同情况看起来完全不同。客户的会话 ID 被查找。完整的对话痕迹出现: 每个用户消息,每个 system prompt 版本 (它们演变),每个 LLM 调用与完整 prompt 和 completion,每个工具调用与输入和输出,每步的延迟,每个 LLM 调用的 token 计数,在调用时活跃的模型版本。调查在分钟内可能。根本原因被识别 (例如,在那个调用中检索从过时的政策版本拉取),修复部署到生产中。客户被以正确的信息跟进。

需要这种可观察性的纪律是真实的。每个 LLM 调用记录 prompt 加 completion,平均可能为 5KB。10,000 每日调用产生每天 50MB,每年 18GB 仅仅是 prompt 数据。保留政策必须考虑这一点。访问控制必须考虑数据敏感性 (一些对话包含 PII)。PII 编辑必须为可以共享的较低敏感日志而工作。

集成跨多个供应商。LLM 调用通过 Bedrock,所以 Bedrock 日志是一层。Embedding 模型可能是 OpenAI 直接,所以那是另一层。工具调用到 Qantas 内部 API,所以那是 Qantas 监控基础设施。Vector DB 查询到 OpenSearch,所以那是另一组日志。可观察性是关于跨多个供应商正常一致编织所有这些。

最成熟的 Qantas AI 项目从第一天起将完整可观察性视为不可协商。Langfuse 或 Datadog LLM 可观察性或类似工具部署在生产之前,而不是在事件之后。Prompt 和 completion 数据流入访问控制的日志存储。PII 编辑在管道中。所有信号的仪表板可供产品所有者和工程师每天查看。

对 AI 交付来说,启示是可观察性是分离的 AI 项目可以在生产中长期生存与的项目在事件中。它感觉像可以推迟的开销,直到第一次客户事件,然后突然团队 wishes 他们一直在投资。从范围确定时把可观察性作为基础要求的交付从业者构建了在生产现实接触中生存的项目。把它当作以后的附加组件的人构建那些没有的项目。
